learn.rule.heading: How this journey is chosen
learn.rule.events: Steps are the {kinds} whose recorded name contains the word {words}.
learn.rule.events_follow.one: Also the events and stories the record links to one of those by {links}.
learn.rule.events_follow.other: Also the events and stories the record links to them by {links}, up to {n} links away.
learn.follow.date_anchor: a before or after link on a recorded date
learn.rule.people: Steps are the people with a recorded participation in the {kinds} whose recorded name contains the word {words}: {records}a claim of the kind {claims}.
learn.rule.people_records: a participation record stored on the event, or
learn.rule.people_follow.one: Events the record links to those by {links} count too.
learn.rule.people_follow.other: Events the record links to those by {links}, up to {n} links away, count too.
learn.rule.also_show: Claims of the kind {kinds} are shown beside a person's records, but never choose anyone.
learn.rule.set_apart: People whose every record carries the marker {markers} are listed apart, after the steps.
learn.rule.stories: Steps are the stories in the part of the story document whose title contains the word {words} ({parts}), with the people and groups each story names.
learn.rule.separate_records: A story and an event with a similar name are separate records here. The journey does not treat them as the same occurrence; whether they are is for scholars to decide.
learn.rule.order_conflict: Some before and after links in the record contradict each other, so the order below leaves them out.
learn.order.recorded: Order: by recorded dates and by the before and after links the record holds; a part follows the event it is part of. Where the record gives no order, steps with a recorded date come first, by date, then stories in reading order, then the rest by name. Each step says which applies.
learn.order.prophet_first_then_name: Order: the Prophet ﷺ first, then everyone else by name, A to Z. The order is not a ranking.
learn.order.name: Order: by name, A to Z. The order is not a ranking.
learn.order.story: Order: the document's own reading order.
learn.steps.heading: The steps
learn.legend.events: Each step links to its page. Under it: why the step is here, where it sits in the order, and the claims about it, each with its status. “Proposed” means put forward but not yet checked by a scholar; “accepted” means a scholar has accepted it.
learn.legend.people: Each step links to the person's page and lists the records behind it, each with its status and source. A participation record stored on an event carries no status: no review of it is recorded.
learn.legend.stories: Each step is a story: read it first, then open the list of the people and groups it names, each link with its status.

learn.index.title: Learn
learn.index.lead: Learning paths through the record, and practice questions. Every step links to its page and shows how far the claims behind it have been checked.
learn.index.draft_note: Every journey here is a draft: the maintainer and the scholars' review board have not yet approved them.
learn.index.no_account: No account is needed. If you mark steps as done, your progress is kept only in this browser.
learn.index.practice_lead: Questions made only from claims that scholars have accepted.
learn.index.how_rules: Each journey is chosen by written rules over the record, never by hand, and its page shows the rules in plain words.
learn.index.how_status: Every claim shows its status: proposed, under review or accepted. Nothing is shown as checked unless a scholar has accepted it.
learn.index.how_doors: Study journeys show the evidence first. Discover journeys show the story first, with the evidence one tap below.
learn.practice.title: Practice
learn.practice.lead: Question prompts made from the record. Every question is built only from claims that scholars have accepted, and every answer shows the claims and sources it rests on.
learn.practice.empty: No questions yet. Questions appear here only after scholars accept claims.
learn.practice.empty_why: A question may rest only on claims that a scholar has accepted. No claim in the record has been accepted yet, so there is nothing to ask. Proposed, under review and rejected claims never make a question.
learn.practice.counts: The record holds {total} claims: {accepted} accepted, {under_review} under review, {proposed} proposed, {rejected} rejected.
learn.practice.answer_note: According to the accepted claims in this record. The record may be incomplete: someone missing here is not recorded, not shown to be absent.
learn.practice.how_accepted: Only claims whose status is “accepted” are used. Proposed, under review, rejected and superseded claims, and links recorded without a status, are never used.
learn.practice.how_join: Each question joins two accepted claims, such as two claims that the same person took part in two events.
learn.practice.how_no_choice: There are no multiple-choice options: a wrong option would say that someone was not somewhere, and no claim says that.
learn.practice.how_contrary: If any claim that has not been rejected says that a person was absent from an event, that person is left out of every answer about that event: a contested matter is never shown as settled.
